S. B. REGISTRY

SECRET

CONFIDENTIAL October 14, 35.

DC(S.B.)
7th

Dear Sir John,

With regard to your note of October 12, 1935 I
send attached hereto a report from the Special Branch
on the subject of Police action in regard to book stores
in the Settlement selling anti-Japanese and other literature
likely to cause a breach of the peace or political compli-
cations.

In the middle of this year, after discussion with
the Secretary-General, it was decided to take action against
all newspapers, chiefly of the mosquito variety, not
registered with the Chinese Authorities. This type of
paper was publishing with impunity inflammatory articles
of an anti-Japanese nature, anti-Government nature, and
so-forth. Action taken was in every case put before the
competent court and future action based on the result of
such prosecution.

I think it improbable that there is any great extort-
ion by Chinese members of the Municipal Police engaged on
this work. There is no doubt considerable difficulty to
be encountered if such efforts at extortion are made in
that it is well known that agents of the Japanese and
Chinese Authorities, and agents of the Bureau of Education

致特别股副巡官（DC(S.B.)）
第七号

尊敬的约翰爵士：

关于您1935年10月12日的便函，现随函附上特别股就警务处针对租界内书店出售反日及其他可能引发破坏和平或政治纠纷的文献所采取行动一事提交的报告。

今年年中，经与总秘书讨论后，决定对所有未向中国当局注册的报纸（主要是那些微不足道的“蚊子报”）采取行动。此类报纸肆无忌惮地刊登具有反日性质、反政府性质等煽动性文章。所采取的行动在每种情况下均提交至有管辖权的法庭，并依据此类起诉的结果决定后续行动。

我认为，参与此项工作的华籍警务处人员大肆勒索的可能性不大。如果确实存在此类勒索企图，无疑会遇到相当大的困难，因为众所周知，日本和中国当局的特工以及教育局的特工

is very improbable shopkeepers will pay the Municipal

Police action re book stores in Settlement.
Communication from H.B.M. Consul-General re.
// and D.S.I. Macao

Sir,
With reference to the attached communication dated
October 12, 1938, from H.B.M. Consul-General, and the
instructions of the D.C. (Special Branch) appended thereon,
submitted herewith is a report on the matter in question.
The efforts of the Municipal Police to prevent the
sale in the Settlement of literature hostile to the Chinese
Government are supplemented by the Bureau of Public Safety
and the local representative of the Ministry of Education
whose officers make frequent visits to local book stores.
When agents of the Municipal Police discover improper
books, the objectionable parts are translated and submitted
to the Legal Department before any action is taken.
When representatives of the extra-Settlement bureaux
discover objectionable books or magazines on sale, they apply
direct to the Shanghai Special District Court for warrants
and co-operate with the Municipal Police when these instruments
are being executed.
There is also good reason to believe that a check is
being kept on literature offered for sale in the Settlement
by agents of the Japanese Authorities.
In view of the activities of the agents of the Japanese
and Chinese Authorities, there is reason to believe that
relaxation of the efforts of the Municipal Police would not
bring any relief to the book stores. On the other hand, it
would leave the Municipal Police open to charges of
inefficiency and would lend colour to the charges already
being made about extortion.
The examination of book stores is now undertaken by
page_data.zh:
S.S 特别股 /////
1938年10月14日。
关于租界内书店的警务行动。
英国总领事来函及 D.S.I. Macao

先生：

参照附件中1938年10月12日英国总领事的来函，以及附于其上的特别股副巡官（D.C. (Special Branch)）的指示，现就此事项提交报告。
警务处为防止在租界内出售敌视中国政府的文献所做的努力，得到了公共安全局和教育部当地代表的补充，后者的官员经常走访当地书店。
当警务处特工发现不当书籍时，在有争议的部分被翻译并提交给法律部之前，不会采取任何行动。
当租界外各局的代表发现正在出售的可疑书籍或杂志时，他们直接向上海特区法院申请搜查令，并在执行这些法律文书时与警务处合作。
也有充分理由相信，日本当局的特工正在对租界内待售的文献进行监控。
鉴于日本和中国当局特工的活动，有理由相信，放松警务处的努力并不会给书店带来任何缓解。另一方面，这将使警务处面临效率低下的指责，并为已经提出的关于勒索的指控提供口实。
目前对书店的检查由

(8)

two Chinese detectives attached to S.S, and their work is
supervised by clerks from the same section. Both the
detectives and clerks of S.S pose as potential customers
when visiting stores, and a check is maintained on their
work by agents and detectives of S.I who are constantly on
the look out for evidence of the existence of anti-Government
and anti-Foreign agitation. Any arrangement which any
member of the Municipal Police might make to allow the sale
of improper books would moreover be likely to break down in
view of the inquiries being made by the Public Safety Bureau
or other interested authorities. The keepers of book stores
are all intelligent people who realise that the Printers and
Publishers Association to which they invariably belong, is
a very influential body. It is therefore very unlikely that
they would tamely agree to the payments of exactions which
did not bring them any benefit.

In executing the orders of the Acting Commissioner
of Police regarding the registration of newspapers and
periodicals Foreign members of the staff of the Special
Branch frequently come into contact with book store keepers,
and so far no complaints have been made to them.

Since the "New Life Weekly" Incident, the measures
to prevent the circulation in the Settlement of anti-Japanese
literature have been carried out more consistently and
vigorously than previously, and six persons have been
successfully prosecuted.

There is no doubt that the members of the Printing
and Publishing Trade have for many years been making
considerable profits by catering to the spirit of hostility
page_data.zh:
(8)

隶属于 S.S 的两名华籍侦探承担，他们的工作由该部门的文员监督。S.S 的侦探和文员在走访书店时均伪装成潜在顾客，而 S.I 的特工和侦探则对他们的工作进行监督，后者不断寻找存在反政府和反外国煽动活动的证据。此外，鉴于公共安全局或其他相关当局正在进行的调查，任何警务处成员为允许出售不当书籍而达成的安排都很可能会破裂。书店老板都是聪明人，他们意识到自己 invariably 所属的印刷出版公会是一个非常有影响力的团体。因此，他们不太可能顺从地同意支付那些不能给他们带来任何好处的勒索款项。

在执行代理警务处长关于报纸和期刊注册的命令时，特别股的外籍职员经常与书店老板接触，迄今为止尚未收到针对他们的投诉。

自“《新生》周刊事件”以来，防止反日文献在租界内流通的措施比以往更加一致和有力，已有六人被成功起诉。

毫无疑问，印刷出版业的成员多年来一直通过迎合公众对

page_data.en:
(3)

to Japan and other Foreign countries, and lecherous inclinations
of the Chinese public. Sufferance of the continuance of this
state of affairs has proved a lucrative source of profit to some
employees of the Ministry of Education.

It came to light in September 1930 that one Chen Te-
tseng (陳德徵) who was local representative of the Ministry of
Education from April 1929 to September 1930, had during that
period amassed a fortune of $300,000. Chen was found guilty
of malfeasance in office and had to resign various appointments
which he held concurrently.

The efforts of the Municipal Police have always
limited the opportunities of the employees of the Department
of Education to make money by venial practices in the Settlement,
and in recent months have undoubtedly been more successful in
this respect than hitherto. The statement of the Minister of
Education about extortion by the Municipal Police is probably
based on reports received from some of the employees of his
Department who consider that their personal interests will be
seriously affected if the present measures taken by the
Municipal Police are maintained.

D. S. I.

D. C. (Special Branch).

Peking C.I. The Board discussed Cases against some
proprietors who were charged in September with
selling anti-Japanese literature. It is only in cases
which are apparently more serious than these that
prosecutions will be brought in future. The position,
however, may be changed if the Japanese complain again.
11/10/35 (Sd.) J. L. C. (J.L.C.)
page_data.zh:
(3)

日本及其他外国的敌对情绪以及中国公众的淫秽倾向来获取巨额利润。容忍这种状态的持续存在已被证明是教育部一些员工的有利可图的收入来源。

1930年9月查明，陈德徵（Chen Te-tseng）在1929年4月至1930年9月期间担任教育部当地代表，在此期间积累了30万元的财富。陈被判犯有渎职罪，并不得不辞去他同时担任的各项职务。

警务处的努力一直限制着教育部员工在租界内通过轻微违规行为牟利的机会，而且在最近几个月里，在这方面无疑比以往更加成功。教育部长关于警务处勒索的声明，可能基于其部门某些员工收到的报告，这些员工认为，如果维持警务处目前采取的措施，他们的个人利益将受到严重影响。

D. S. I.

特别股副巡官（D. C. (Special Branch)）。

北京刑事情报科。董事会讨论了一些业主的案件，这些人因在九月被控出售反日文献而被起诉。只有在这种情况下，未来才会提起诉讼，即案件显然比这些更严重。然而，如果日本人再次投诉，情况可能会改变。
1935年10月11日 （签名） J. L. C. (J.L.C.)

BRITISH CONSULATE-GENERAL,
P.O. BOX 259. SHANGHAI.
October 12th, 1935.

Personal and confidential

Dear Bourne,

The Chinese Minister of Education has recently
approached me indirectly and very confidentially on
the following matter. It is stated that under Japanese
pressure the municipal police are undertaking the
investigation of publications by Chinese publishing
companies to see if they contain anti-Japanese
propaganda. I am assured that the Chinese Government
have already taken strict measures in the way of
censorship and would deal with such cases themselves.
The Minister asks me unofficially therefore for my
good offices to obtain a relaxation by the municipal
police of their activities in this direction. It is
also alleged that some members of the police are
making the investigation an opportunity for extortion.

With regard to the latter charge the answer of
course is that if any evidence is produced you will
/be

Major K.M. Bourne, M.C.,
Acting Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
SHANGHAI.

英国驻上海总领事馆，

1935年10月12日。

私人且机密

亲爱的伯恩：

中国教育部长最近就以下事项间接且非常机密地与我接洽。据称，在日本人的压力下，工部局警务处正在调查中国出版公司的出版物，以查看其中是否含有反日宣传内容。我得到保证，中国政府已经采取了严格的审查措施，并将自行处理此类案件。因此，部长非正式地请求我从中斡旋，以使工部局警务处放松在此方面的活动。此外，还有人指控警务处某些成员利用调查之机进行勒索。

Personal and confidential October 12th, 1935. 


Dear Bourne, 

The Chinese Minister of Education has recently 
approached me indirectly and very confidentially on 
the following matter. It is stated that under Japanese 
pressure the municipal police are undertaking the 
investigation of publications by Chinese publishing 
companies to see if they contain anti-Japanese 
propaganda. I am assured that the Chinese Government 
have already taken strict measures in the way of 
censorship and would deal with such cases themselves. 
The Minister asks me unofiicially therefore for my 
good offices to obtain a relaxation by the municipal 
police of their activities in this direction. It is 
also alleged that some members of the police are 
making the investigation an opportunity for extortion. 

With regard to the latter charge the answer of
